question: Determine the vector, Cartesian and intercept forms of the plane passing through $P(1,2,-1)$ and perpendicular to the line joining $A(2,-1,3)$ and $B(4,2,-1)$.
explanation:
Direction of the Normal
The direction ratios of the line joining $A(2,-1,3)$ and $B(4,2,-1)$ are
$$4-2,\quad 2-(-1),\quad -1-3$$
that is,
$$2,3,-4$$
Since the required plane is perpendicular to this line, $2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ is a normal vector to the plane.

Vector Equation
The position vector of $P(1,2,-1)$ is $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. Hence, the vector equation of the plane is
$$\left[\vec{r}-(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})\right]\cdot(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k})=0$$

Cartesian Equation
Writing $\vec{r}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ gives
$$2(x-1)+3(y-2)-4(z+1)=0$$
Therefore,
$$2x+3y-4z=12$$

Intercept Form
Dividing throughout by $12$,
$$\frac{x}{6}+\frac{y}{4}-\frac{z}{3}=1$$
Thus, the intercepts on the coordinate axes are $6$, $4$ and $-3$ respectively.

Final Result
The vector equation is $\left[\vec{r}-(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})\right]\cdot(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k})=0$, the Cartesian equation is $2x+3y-4z=12$, and the intercept form is $\frac{x}{6}+\frac{y}{4}-\frac{z}{3}=1$.

options.A: Vector: $[\vec r-(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)]\cdot(2\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k)=0$; Cartesian: $2x-3y+4z=-8$; intercept: $\frac{x}{-4}+\frac{y}{8/3}+\frac{z}{-2}=1$
options.B: Vector: $[\vec r-(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)]\cdot(2\hat i+3\hat j+4\hat k)=0$; Cartesian: $2x+3y+4z=4$; intercept: $\frac{x}{2}+\frac{y}{4/3}+\frac{z}{1}=1$
options.C: Vector: $[\vec r-(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)]\cdot(2\hat i+3\hat j-4\hat k)=0$; Cartesian: $2x+3y-4z=6$; intercept: $\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{2}-\frac{z}{3/2}=1$
